extracted.intended_audience: prospective Russell Sage Foundation (RSF) core grant applicants / grant seekers / researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Describes RSF's application intake and multi-stage review process for Core Research Grants, including internal LOI screening, external peer review, advisory committee consideration, and final decision authority based on budget. Useful for applicants preparing LOIs and full proposals to RSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress conditional on positive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: *Progress at each step of the review process is conditional on positive reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement from LOI to external review to advisory committee and Board/President consideration depends on favorable outcomes at each stage; negative reviews at any stage can halt progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal LOI screening (staff reviewers and screening criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 3 members of the RSF program staff read every LOI submitted – we are primarily looking for fit with the foundation, clarity in presentation, and whether the data and methods are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The internal screen is focused on (1) fit with RSF program areas, (2) clarity of the LOI, and (3) adequate description of data and methods. LOIs that do not meet these expectations are not advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI outcome if failing internal screen
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs that do not pass the internal screen are declined without comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure LOIs clearly demonstrate fit, present ideas concisely, and describe data/methods sufficiently to avoid an un-commented decline at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI external review minimum reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs that pass the internal screen are sent out for external review – a minimum of 3 reviewers read every LOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers provide substantive assessments that inform staff decisions about which projects to invite for full proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff decision informed by external reviewer recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the recommendations of these external reviewers, RSF program staff decide which projects to invite for full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers' evaluations are a key input; applicants should aim to satisfy criteria external reviewers typically assess (importance, rigor, feasibility, data/methods clarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal external review composition
rubrics_metrics.description: When invited proposals are received, they are sent to the same reviewers who reviewed the LOI (when possible), plus up to 2 additional external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full proposals are generally reviewed by a largely overlapping set of reviewers to preserve continuity, with up to two additional experts added; expect multiple external assessments of the full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee review and decision role
rubrics_metrics.description: When the external review process is complete, all materials are provided to standing Advisory Committees. Advisory committee members are external to the Foundation and recruited specifically for their expertise in each of the Foundation’s program area. Advisory committees decide which proposals are moved forward to RSF Board for funding consideration, which proposals are invited to resubmit, and which proposals are declined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committees synthesize external reviews and staff materials to make recommendations about advancing, inviting resubmission, or declining proposals; applicants should ensure proposals address likely committee concerns and clearly document methods and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final authority by budget level (Trustee vs Presidential Grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects with budgets greater than $75,000 (Trustee Grants), the RSF Board serves as final authority. For projects with budgets of up to $75,000 (Presidential Grants), the RSF President serves as final authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the vast majority of proposals that reach the Board are approved for funding, the Board may reject a proposal, request or offer a revision, ask for further clarification, or approve with conditions. Applicants should be prepared for possible Board- or President-level requests for revision or clarification at the final decision stage.
